preamble: Solutions to all partial and some complete clues are members (in some cases partial) of a single body of work.

clue.text: Copy cat, perhaps, is brought in to tickle one's fancy

indicators.note: the pieces before this phrase are placed inside the word for copy, so it works as a container signal

parts.note: to ape is to copy or mimic
a cat is one example of a pet, hence 'perhaps'
taken as written

explanation.surface: A copycat performance meant to amuse someone and win them over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copy cat' reads as one idea, a copycat, but splits into two pieces: copy and cat.
explanation.definitionFit: To whet someone's appetite is to stir their desire, which matches tickling their fancy.

clue.text: Patchable one set in order

indicators.note: to set something is to arrange it, so these letters are put into a new arrangement

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Someone sets a repairable item back in its proper place.
explanation.walkthrough: PATCHABLE plus I gives ten letters, which 'set' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Arranged according to the letters A, B, C means arranged in order, the sequence of the alphabet.

clue.text: Continuity of topless native amidst change

indicators.note: amidst means in the middle of, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: small change in British money is pence, coins

indicators.note: losing its top means the first letter of the word for native is removed

parts.note: a German is a native of Germany

explanation.surface: A local person without a shirt is somehow steady through a period of transition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' looks like part of the definition's surface sense of transition, but it is the British coins. 'topless' drops the opening letter of the native's nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: Permanence is the state of lasting unchanged, which is continuity over time.

clue.text: It charges for tailless fish

indicators.note: without its tail means the last letter of the fish is dropped

parts.note: the turbot is a flatfish

explanation.surface: A creature attacks in exchange for a fish with no tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It charges' is a cryptic look at a turbocharger, a device that forces air into an engine.
explanation.definitionFit: A turbo is short for turbocharger, a device that charges an engine with compressed air.

clue.text: Spot toys?

parts.note: the word spot is what you get when the letters of tops spin round, reading backwards

explanation.surface: A child is told to pick out the playthings.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: spin the word TOPS and it reads SPOT, the clue's first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tops that spin on a point are classic children's playthings, so they are toys.

clue.text: Exhibitor taking small fall

definitions.meaning: one who shows something, an exhibitor

explanation.surface: An exhibitor picks up a minor tumble at the show.
explanation.definitionFit: One who shows is a show-er, and a brief burst of rain is a light fall of precipitation.

clue.text: Playwright pursuing he-man's young bird

indicators.note: pursuing means coming after, so the playwright follows the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
Ron is a man's name
George Bernard Shaw, the Irish playwright

explanation.surface: A dramatist chases after a muscleman's chick.
explanation.definitionFit: A heronshaw is an old word for a heron, especially a young one, which is a bird.

clue.text: Come to watch

definitions.meaning: to come to is to regain consciousness or rouse from sleep
a vigil kept over a dead body before burial

explanation.definitionFit: To rouse from sleep is to regain consciousness, and a vigil beside a corpse is a traditional Irish watch.

clue.text: Insignificant item of litter

parts.note: looks like a bit of rubbish dropped in the street, but means the smallest, weakest animal born in a litter

explanation.definitionFit: The runt is the undersized, least significant member of a newborn litter of animals.

clue.text: One painting about to get left outside

indicators.note: the word for left goes outside the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
painting is art

explanation.surface: Someone working on a painting is about to have their left side exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: The ship's left side cuts open after its R to take the reversed piece. This is the first word of Joyce's A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man.
explanation.definitionFit: Joyce's novel A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man opens its title with this word, so it belongs to the theme.

clue.text: Tamed, all right, when flanked by gun

indicators.note: to be flanked is to have something on either side, so the gun goes round the other piece

parts.note: the Bren is a British light machine gun
OK means all right

explanation.surface: Something is made docile and fine when guns stand on either side.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse that has been broken is one tamed and trained to accept a rider.

clue.text: Gruesome obi egghead plotted to introduce to class

indicators.note: plotted means schemed or worked out, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the head of the word egg is its first letter

explanation.surface: A clever person schemes to bring a horrid Japanese sash into polite society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plotted' rearranges GRUESOME plus OBI into EMBOURGEOIS; E from 'egghead' completes it. 'egghead' looks like an intellectual.
explanation.definitionFit: To embourgeoise is to make someone middle-class, bringing them into the bourgeois social class.

clue.text: A measure of influence: love to castrate without force

parts.note: to have a say is to have some influence
love is zero in tennis, written O

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the word for castrate goes round the other piece

parts.note: to unman is to castrate
G is the symbol for the force of gravity

explanation.surface: Someone weighs their influence and threatens to geld a man without using force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' puts G inside UNMAN; old-fashioned 'without' meant outside. It ends the title of Joyce's A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man.
explanation.definitionFit: These three words close the title of Joyce's novel A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man, the theme.

clue.text: Parting words an insult about Cummings exercise

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the insult goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a slight is an insult
e e cummings, the American poet who wrote his name in lower case
PT is physical training, exercise

explanation.surface: A farewell jibe aimed at the workout routine of someone called Cummings.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying goodnight with this phrase is what people say when parting at bedtime.

clue.text: Instruments required for chap to act script

parts.note: a chap is a man
to do is to act
an actor's script is their lines

explanation.surface: A fellow needs a script before he can perform on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandoline, also spelt mandolin, is a stringed musical instrument.

clue.text: Fix Shed in conclusion

indicators.note: in means inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a conclusion is an end
Shed is the setter, so in the setter's voice Shed means me

explanation.surface: A garden shed gets repaired at the end of the job.
explanation.walkthrough: Shed is the pseudonym of this puzzle's setter, so Shed means ME.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to correct its errors, or fix it.

clue.text: Call ships

parts.note: to dub someone is to call them by a name
liners are large passenger ships

explanation.surface: A request to telephone some vessels.
explanation.walkthrough: Dubliners is Joyce's collection of short stories; the clue has no definition beyond the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Joyce's 1914 collection of short stories about life in Ireland's capital bears this title, part of the theme.

clue.text: Unexpectedly phone one back — sicken of passion for novelty

indicators.note: unexpectedly means in a surprising way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: back means the next word is read backwards

parts.note: to ail is to sicken

explanation.surface: A surprise phone call back makes someone sick of their passion for new things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unexpectedly' rearranges PHONE into NEOPH, and 'back' turns AIL into LIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Neophilia is a love of new things, a craving for novelty.

clue.text: Egg warmer in island hill

parts.note: Cuba is a Caribbean island
a tor is a rocky hill

explanation.surface: Someone keeps eggs warm on a hill on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: An incubator is a device that keeps eggs warm until they hatch.

clue.text: Handle savage oriental invasion

indicators.note: an invasion is one thing entering another, so one letter goes inside the word for savage

parts.note: wild means savage
E stands for east, the oriental direction

explanation.surface: Someone copes with a brutal invasion from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: To wield a tool or weapon is to handle it and use it.

clue.text: Effective outcome of simple men talking

indicators.note: the answer comes out of the words that follow, which contain it

explanation.surface: An effective result of plain people chatting.
explanation.definitionFit: Implemental means acting as an instrument, so it is effective in bringing something about.

clue.text: Boredom that's about to engulf itinerant nun

indicators.note: to engulf is to swallow up, so one piece goes round the other
about means turned round, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: i.e. stands for id est, that is

indicators.note: itinerant means wandering, so these letters move around

explanation.surface: Weariness is set to swallow up a wandering nun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the abbreviation round, and 'itinerant' scrambles the nun before 'to engulf' wraps the turned piece around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is a feeling of listless dissatisfaction from lack of interest, which is boredom.

clue.text: A short turn-up for the girl

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: rev is short for revolution, a turn

explanation.surface: A brief upturned hem for a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn-up' reads like the fold at the bottom of trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Vera is a girl's name, so it stands for the girl.

clue.text: Member of race said to be chosen

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the word sounds like the answer

parts.note: picked means chosen

explanation.surface: A member of a team is said to have been selected.
explanation.definitionFit: The Picts were an ancient people of northern Scotland, so one is a member of that race.

clue.text: Old dears — about 49

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the old dears go round the number

parts.note: former partners or sweethearts are exes
IL is a Roman numeral reading of 49, one less than fifty

explanation.surface: Elderly ladies of around 49 years.
explanation.walkthrough: IL for 49 is an informal Roman numeral; the strict form is XLIX. Exiles is Joyce's only play.
explanation.definitionFit: Joyce's only stage play, first published in 1918, carries this title, making it a member of the theme.

clue.text: Northerner with point to go on and on about

parts.note: a Finn comes from Finland in northern Europe
E is east, a point of the compass

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for go on and on is read backwards

parts.note: to nag is to go on and on at someone

explanation.surface: A northern person with a point to keep repeating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns NAG into GAN. It is the first word of Joyce's Finnegans Wake, the second word being 7-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Joyce's final novel is Finnegans Wake, and this name is its first word, completed by 7-down.

clue.text: His traits are revealed in a 9

definitions.text: His traits are revealed in a 9

indicators.note: revealed suggests letters that are uncovered in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A painted likeness shows off someone's character.
explanation.walkthrough: TRAITS rearranged gives the answer, and a 9-across (portrait) shows its painter's traits; it also fits Joyce's title.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter's personality shows through in a portrait, so this is the person whose traits it reveals.

clue.text: Compiler has turned into fruit — hence, is abnormal

indicators.note: into means inside, so one piece goes within the fruit

parts.note: dates are fruit

indicators.note: turned means read the other way round

parts.note: the compiler is the setter, so 'Compiler has' gives I've

explanation.surface: The puzzle-setter has become a fruit, which is strange.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter often calls themselves 'compiler', so 'Compiler has' gives I'VE; 'turned' reverses it before it goes into the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: To deviate is to depart from the norm, so something that deviates is abnormal.
